resources.title: Who is God
resources.description: Theme: GOD AND HIS CREATION | Content: 1. Who is God? (Supreme being, the Creator of the universe, etc.) Gen. 1:1; Jer. 10:12 2. Attributes of God (Sovereign creator, omnipresence, invisible, only wise God, Spirit), etc. 3. Names of God in different Nigerian languages e.g. Ubangiji (Hausa), Olorun (Yoruba), Chineke (Igbo), Abasi (Efik), Tamara (Ijaw), Shekwo (Gbagyi), Soko (Nupe) etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain who God is; 2. list some attributes of God; 3. give the names of God in different Nigerian languages.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides the students to discuss who God is. 2. Guides students to list and discuss the attributes of God. 3. Asks the students to mention the names of God in their own language.

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion on who God is. 2. List and discuss the attributes of God. 3. Give names of God in their different languages. 4. Copy points into their note books. 5. Ask and answer questions.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible 2. Word cards of names of God in Different Nigerian languages.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state who God is; 2. list five attributes of God; 3. write the names of God in five Nigerian languages.

resources.title: God’s Creation
resources.description: Theme: GOD AND HIS CREATION | Content: 1. Biblical account of the creation. Gen. 1 & 2. 2. Why God created human beings: (know, worship, serve him), etc. 3. Songs about creation in English and different Nigerian languages (e.g. all things bright and beautiful, the Lord God made them all).
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. give sequential account of the Biblical narration on the creation of the world; 2. state the purpose of the creation of human beings; 3. narrate the account of the first set of human beings created by God.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tell the story of creation. 2. Leads students to read the story. 3. Explains and discusses reason why God made man and woman. 4. Guides students to differentiate between living beings and non-living things.

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion on God’s creation. 2. Read and search Bible passages on creation. 3. Tell stories about creation. 4. Copy points into notes 5. Sing songs 6. Draw things created by God.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible 2. Biography showing sequence of creation 3. Students as human resources. 4. Natural school environme nt showing trees, birds, soil, rocks, stones etc.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give an orderly Biblical account of the creation from day one to day six; 2. narrate the story of the creation of man and woman; 3. state at least two reasons why God made human beings.

resources.title: Human Beings Share in God’s Creative Activities
resources.description: Theme: GOD AND HIS CREATION | Content: 1. Sharing in God’s creative activities through Marriage; Jn.2:1 -The meaning of marriage – Gen. 2:22 – 25. Eph. 5: 21 – 31. 2. Purposes of marriage companionship, procreation, Gen.1:28 responsibility, preventing immorality, STDs, HIV Virus/AIDS, etc. 3. Things invented by man e.g. cars, chairs, aeroplanes, buildings, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of the term “marriage”; 2. mention the purpose of marriage; 3. explain that, despite the problems of homo-sexuality, God made marriage to be between man and woman; 4. list things made by man.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read relevant Bible passages. 2. Guides students in discussing ways marriages prevent immorality and the spread of STDs, HIV/AIDS Virus, etc. 3. Guides game on identification of things made by man. 4. Takes students on field trips to churches, maternity homes, hills and teach them birth and wedding songs.

Students: 1. Watch and appreciate wedding pictures. 2. Participates in class discussion 3. Sing and dance to marriage and birth songs; 4. Read Bible passages; 5. Copy chalk board summaries into their notes and role play wedding ceremonies; 6. Go on field trips and discuss observations during field trips.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible 2. Bible Pictures. 3. Word and sentence card 4. Wedding discussion. 5. Costumes 6. Learners’ environment 7. Artificial flowers, bird, dolls, etc. 8. Invitation cards to weddings. 9. Audio visual materials of wedding songs and music.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give the meaning of marriage; 2. state two functions of marriage; 3. give two reasons why man should not marry his fellow man and vice versa; 4. list three things made by man.

resources.title: Disobedience
resources.description: Theme: GOD AND HIS CREATION | Content: 1. Biblical account of first human disobedience. Gen 3: 1 – 19 2. Consequences of Adam and Eve’s disobedience. Gen 3: 14 -19 3. Acts of disobedience and its consequences
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify disobedience as sin; 2. give Biblical account of first human disobedience; 3. enumerate their own acts of disobedience and consequences; 4. identify consequences of disobedience against the national laws e.g. vandalization of public properties, disobeying traffic light, etc.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains meaning of disobedience. 2. Leads students to recognize disobedience as sin. 3. Guides students to read Bible passages. 4. Guides students to respect and obey the laws of the nation using the national pledge.

Students: 1. Read individually the Bible passages. 2. Participate and copy down points in their notes. 3. Write apology letter to parents. Bring reports of parent’s feelings at receiving apology letters. 4. Recite national pledge.
resources.resources: 1. Educational television. 2. Film strips 3. The Bible. 4. Projectors. 5. Students as learning resources. 6. Printed or written copy of the national pledge.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the term disobedience; 2. give a Biblical account of the first human disobedience; 3. mention two consequence of Adam and Eve’s disobedience; 4. state three acts of disobedience common among Nigerian youths today.

resources.title: Reconciliation
resources.description: Theme: GOD AND HIS CREATION | Content: 1. Meaning of reconciliation. 2. Conditions necessary for reconciliation e.g. Father of the prodigal son reconciles with his son Lk. 15:11-32. 3. Ways of reconciling with offenders (Shake hands, hug, say I am sorry, give gifts, forgive etc). eg Esau reconciles with Jacob Gen. 33 1-11.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the meaning of reconciliation and identify conditions necessary for reconciliations; 2. narrate the story of the prodigal son; 3. list and demonstrate ways of reconciliation; 4. recount the story of Jacobs’s reconciliation with Esau.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains reconciliation. 2. Guides students to identify conditions necessary for reconciliation. 3. Vividly narrates the story of the prodigal son. 4. Reads and guides students to read relevant Bible passages. 5. Plays recorded songs depicting conditions of the prodigal son. “comeback home to the waiting arms of the Father”

Students: 1. Listen and write down definition. 2. Participate in reading the Bible. 3. Listen, sing, dance, role-play etc.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures of quarreling friends reconciling. 2. Records of songs e.g. when the going is good and fair, etc. Come back home to the waiting arms of the father 3. Illustrations showing land marks in prodigal son’s lives. 4. Costume. 5. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define reconciliation; 2. give three reasons for reconciliation; 3. narrate the story of the prodigal son; 4. state two ways we can reconcile with our offenders.

resources.title: Relation- ship in the Family
resources.description: Theme: RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND MAN | Content: 1. Meaning and types of family 2. Recognition of family members. 3. Different roles of members of the family. Eph. 6: 1-9, Eph. 5: 21 – 33; Col. 3: 18- 21; I Pet. 3:1– 7. 4. Concept of good family name. Prov. 22: 1; Ecc. 17: 1
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. mention the different types of families; 2. mention names of their family members and draw the family tree; 3. Identify roles of members of the family; 4. State the attributes of a good family name.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to draw the family tree. 2. Explains different roles of family members. 3. Explains the attributes of a good family using some known families in the community as examples.

Students: 1. Participates in class discussions. 2. Draw their own family trees. 3. Listen and read in turns the Bible passage. 4. Mention some families in the community with good name.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures of family members. 2. Flash cards bearing names of persons. 3. Drawing showing family tree of Jesus. 4. Students as learning resources. 5. The Holy Bible.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. write names of three members of their family; 2. identify different types of family; 3. mention three roles of members of the family; 4. mention two things that help to maintain a good family name/reputa tion.

resources.title: Relation- ship in School
resources.description: Theme: RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND MAN | Content: 1. Names of members of the school, (School Principals, subject teachers, prefects, Friends, etc). 2. Choosing friends at school (factors: common interest, age, religion, etc.). As example of good friends. 3. As examples of good friends; Friendship between David and Jonathan. I Sam. 18: 1 – 5. 4. Bad friendship leads to cultism, stealing, drug addictions, examination malpractice, prostitution, lesbianism, homosexuality, smoking, drinking, laziness, truancy, etc. Prov. 1: 10; 2Thes. 3: 6 -13.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. write the name of their principals, form master/mistress, subject teachers, etc; 2. identify the factors that aid them in choosing friends; 3. explain why they should choose and maintain good friends; 4. identify the evils of bad friendship.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to list names of principal, teachers etc. 2. Guides students on how to identify genuine friends. 3. Leads students to read relevant Bible passages. 4. Guides students to role-play or (and) mime the story of the friend at midnight. 5. Leads the students to identify evils of bad friendship.

Students: 1. Write down names of teachers and their subject areas. 2. Mention factors that aid them in choosing friends. 3. Mention qualities of good friendship. 4. Mention social evils among youths. 5. Role-play the friend at midnight.
resources.resources: 1. Students and school environment as learning resources. 2. Wall chart showing qualities of genuine friendship. 3. Loaves of bread. 4. Mats. 5. Classroom chair and space. 6. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. make a list of their school teachers; 2. mention two factors to consider when choosing friends; 3. give four reasons why they must choose good friends; 4. list five consequences of choosing bad friends.

resources.title: Relationship in Community and Church
resources.description: Theme: RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND MAN | Content: 1. Identification of the names of community leaders. 2. Ways of sustaining relationships in the community: - respect for elders and leaders, - obeying the laws of the land, - participating in community development programmes, - caring for the needy and religious tolerance. Gal.6:2 3. Relationship in church. - Love your Christian brother and sister etc. Rom. 12:9-21 - Maintaining relationship in church. Heb.10:25, 1Pt.3: 8-13; Rom. 13:1-7
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. identify names of members and leaders in their communities; 2. state ways we maintain relationships in the community; 3. Mention ways to maintain relationship in the church; 4. Write and discuss their observations at field trips.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads students to identify names of some community members. 2. Guides Bible reading of the relevant passages. 3. Takes students on field trips around the community.

Students: 1. Search for information about founders of their community and churches. 2. Read relevant Bible passages. 3. Go on field trips. 4. Discuss observations at field trips.
resources.resources: 1. Posters of needy members of the communities 2. Cartoons and clippings of men giving or denying alms to beggars and destitute. 3. Pictures of rulers, priests, bishops, worshippers, etc. 4. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. write names of three community members and rulers; 2. state three ways we can maintain relationship in community; 3. identify four ways we maintain relationship in the church. 4. discuss observations at field trips.

resources.title: Relationship with God
resources.description: Theme: RELATIONSHIP WITH GOD AND MAN | Content: 1. Relating with God through prayer, reading the Bible worshiping God, praising God, etc. Acts.16:25 2. Ways God talks to us: - our parents - the Bible (His Word) - teachers - priests/ preachers 3. Ways of maintaining good relationship with God: - loving God - loving one another - daily prayer - living holy life - worshiping and doing good - reading the Bible - forgiving one another etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain what “prayer” is; 2. recite the Lords’ prayer and apostle’s creed; 3. mention ways we maintain relationship with God; 4. mention ways God talks to us.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads students to identify books of the Bible. 2. Guides students in meaningfully saying of the Lord’s Prayer and the apostle’s creed. 3. Through questioning leads students in discussing ways of maintaining relationship with God.

Students: 1. Copy out books of the Bible sequentially into their notes. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Learn and sing songs; such as read your Bible pray every day if you want to grow.
resources.resources: 1. Wall charts showing names of God and books of the Bible. 2. Resource persons e.g. priest/ preachers from the local church. 3. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define prayer; 2. recite the Lord’s prayer; 3. write at least three ways we can maintain relationship with God; 4. mention two ways through which God talks to us.

resources.title: Call to Obedience
resources.description: Theme: GOD’S CALL | Content: 1. Meaning of obedience. 2. Blessing from obeying God’s call. Gen. 12:1-9. 3. Abraham demonstrates his obedience: - The birth of Isaac Gen. 21:1 -8. - The “sacrifice” of Isaac Gen. 22:1-19
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the term obedience; 2. narrate the story of the call of Abraham; 3. state the blessings from Abraham’s obedience to God’s call.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides reading of Bible passages 2. Leads discussion on blessings accrued from Abraham’s obedience. 3. Guides and leads the students to dramatize the “sacrifice” of Isaac.

Students: 1. Listen and write down meaning of obedience in their note books 2. Listen and participate in reading. 3. Mention blessings that accrue from obedience 4. Participate and volunteer to act, volunteer to bring costumes and act their roles.
resources.resources: 1. Bible atlases. 2. Picture/pos ters of Abraham leaving Ur of the Chaldeans; sacrifice of Isaac. 3. Costumes. 4. Students as resource persons to act, role play. 5. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give the meaning of obedience; 2. narrate the story of call of Abraham and his response; 3. write three blessings of Abraham for obeying God’s call.

resources.title: Call to Freedom
resources.description: Theme: GOD’S CALL | Content: 1. The meaning and types of freedom. 2. The call of Moses Ex. 3: 1 -15. 3. Deborah and Barak lead their people to freedom Judges 4.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. define freedom; 2. narrate the story of the call of Moses; 3. recount the story of the defeat of the Canaanites led by Deborah.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of freedom. 2. Leads the students to identify aspects of freedom. 3. Leads the students to read Bible passages. 4. Sets up film on “Moses”.

Students: 1. Listen and write down meaning of freedom. 2. Listen and participate in class. discussion. 3. Answering teacher’s questions. 4. View film.
resources.resources: 1. Doll babies and babies clothing; cane cots. 2. Wall charts showing the burning bush. 3. Pictures of pharaoh and his chariots and horsemen being gulped by the sea. 4. The film “Moses”, pictures of Deborah, Students as resource persons. 5. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. define freedom; 2. tell the stories of the call of Moses; 3. give an account of the defeat of the Canaanites by Deborah.

resources.title: Call to Service
resources.description: Theme: GOD’S CALL | Content: 1. Meaning of service. 2. Example of people who served in the Bible. – Joseph in Egypt. Gen. 37:12 -36. - Joseph serves in Egypt. Gen. 41: 37 – 57. - Ruth serves her mother-in-law Ruth 11: 7 – 18. 3. Lessons from the service of Joseph and Ruth. 4. Life in God’s service 1 Pet. 2: 18-25. 5. Problems of service: - Seduction Gen. 39:7 - Bribery & corruption, etc. 6. Reward of service: - Promotion Gen 41:37-43 - Long life
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of services; 2. mention examples of people who served in the Bible; 3. enumerate ways Christians are called to the service of God and humanity and problems of service; 4. explain ways Christians are rewarded for their services.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read Bible passages. 2. Guides students to discover problems and blessing in service. 3. Leads students to deduce lessons from the lives of Joseph and Ruth. 4. Guides students to assess qualities of some Nigerian leaders both past and present.

Students: 1. Read Bible passages. 2. Role-play 3. Participate 4. Copy chalkboard summary. 5. Deduce lessons and write same into their notes.
resources.resources: 1. Students as learning resources. 2. Posters of leaders. 3. Newspapers showing photographs of leaders rendering services to humanity. 4. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. narrate the story of the sale of Joseph into Egypt; 2. recount the story of Ruth’s faithfulness in her service to her mother in-law; 3. give an account of Joseph’s rise from slavery to governorship in Egypt; 4. identify three blessings derived from rendering faithful service.

resources.title: Call to Repentance
resources.description: Theme: GOD’S CALL | Content: 1. King David obeys God’s call to repentance. 2 Sam. 12:7-13; Ps. 51. 2. The people of Nineveh repented of their sins. Jonah 3:1-10. 3. John the Baptist call for repentance Lk. 3:1-14; Matt. 1: 1-12. 4. Jesus Christ’s call for repentance: Mk 1:14-15. 5. Consequences of lack of repentance 1 Sam. 3:18; 4:10-21.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe how David and Zaccheus responded to the call for repentance; 2. given an account of the act of repentance of the Ninevites; 3. identify the demands to repentance on John the Baptist’s hearers; 4. identify and discuss some consequence s of lack of repentance.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to mimic Jonah in Nineveh. 2. Discusses consequences of cultism, examination malpractices, unchastity, smoking, stealing, drunkenness etc as example of lack of repentance. 3. Guides the students to read Bible passages and explains same.

Students: 1. Role play 2. Mimic 3. Read Bible passages. 4. Generate and write down consequen ces of cultism.
resources.resources: 1. Students as learning resources. 2. Costume e.g. crown, ashes, bell etc. 3. Flip charts with song of repentance written on them. 4. Pictures of Zaccheus on the sycamore tree. 5. Cartoons and clippings and posters of consequence of examination malpractices, cultism, unchaste conduct, drunkenness, HIV/AIDS
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give account of the circumstance surrounding Uriah’s death; 2. identify two evidences of the repentance of the Ninevites. 3. list two acts of repentance and significance demanded by John the Baptist; 4. list two consequence of each of the following: i. Cultism, ii. Unchaste conduct, iii. Examination malpractices, iv. Drunkenness, v. Smoking, vi. Stealing, etc.

resources.title: The Birth of Jesus
resources.description: Theme: THE EARLY LIFE OF JESUS | Content: 1. The Annunciation. Isaiah 9:6-7; Matt. 1: 22 & 23; Lk. 1:30-33. 2. The birth of Jesus. Matt. 1:18-25; Lk. 2:1-7. 3. The Shepherds visit. Lk. 2:8-20. 4. The visit of the wise men. Matt. 2:1- 12. 5. The value of virginity before marriage e.g. - Free from STDs - HIV/AIDS - Guilt - Unwanted pregnancy - Abortion - Death
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. mention instances the birth of Jesus was announced; 2. narrate the story of the birth of Jesus; 3. describe the visit of the wise men to Baby Jesus and state the gifts presented to Him; 4. state the value of virginity before marriage.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Initiates and leads class discussion on: - the annunciation - the birth of Jesus; - The visit of the wise men. 2. leads students to dramatize the visit of the shepherds; 3. Explains the nature of Mary’s pregnancy, the meaning and significance of the virgin birth.

Students: 1. Participates in class discussion. 2. Read out relevant Bible passages. 3. Answer teacher’s questions. 4. Dramatize the birth of Jesus. 5. Dramatize the visit of the wise men.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Drama Costumes 3. Charts 4. Pictures. 5. Film strip. 6. Video cassettes. 7. Film projector. 8. Gift during birth and naming ceremonies.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. name the old testament prophet who announced the birth of Jesus; 2. state the town where Jesus was born; 3. list the three presents given to Jesus by the wise men and their significance; 4. list five consequences of sex before marriage.

resources.title: The Presentation of Jesus in the Temple
resources.description: Theme: THE EARLY LIFE OF JESUS | Content: 1. Jesus presented at the temple. Lk. 2:21-24 2. Prophecy of Simeon. Lk.2:25-35 3. Prophecy of Anna. Lk. 2:36- 40.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. mention the importance of the presentation of Jesus at the Temple; 2. describe what happened after the child was presented; 3. state the significance of the prophecies by Simeon and Anna.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on the presentation of Jesus in the temple. 2. Guides students to dramatize the presentation of Jesus in the Temple. 3. Stresses the importance of child’s presentation in the church.

Students: 1. Participates in class discussions, ask and answer questions. 2. Read out relevant Bible passages. 3. Dramatize the presentation of Jesus in the temple. 4. Bring Costumes from their houses.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible Pictures 3. Charts 4. Film. 5. Drama Costumes.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state why Jesus was presented at the Temple; 2. give the name of two people who prophesized about Jesus after the presentation; 3. mention the implication of Simeon’s prophecy to the people of Israel; 4. mention the need for child presentation in the Temple of God.

resources.title: Jesus and His Family
resources.description: Theme: THE EARLY LIFE OF JESUS | Content: 1. Jesus understanding of family. Matt. 12:4, 6-50. 2. Jesus obeyed His parents. Lk. 2:51-52; Eph.6.1:3
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state who are regarded by Jesus as members of “His true” family; 2. explain the importance of obedience to parents and others
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on Jesus and His relations 2. Plays films or video cassettes for students 3. Leads students to discuss various ways of showing obedience.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher and ask questions. 2. Participate in discussion on the need for obedience. 3. Discuss various ways of showing obedience
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible Pictures 3. Bible films
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. name at least three relatives of Jesus; 2. explain who qualifies as “true” member of Jesus family; 3. mention two moral lessons learnt from the life of Jesus Christ among members of His family.

resources.title: The Baptism of Jesus Christ
resources.description: Theme: 1 THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. The Baptism of Jesus. Matt.3:3-17; Matt.1:9-11, Lk.3:21-22. 2. The significance of the Baptism of Jesus 3. The importance of Baptism in the life of Christians.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. narrate the story of Jesus Baptism; 2. state the significance of the Baptism of Jesus; 3. list the importance of Baptism to Christians.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on: - the Baptism of Jesus. - the significance of Baptism. - Importance of Baptism in the life of Christians.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions. 2. Ask and answer questions. 3. Read the Bible passages.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible Pictures 3. Charts 4. Posters and films.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. narrate what happened during the Baptism of Jesus; 2. give two significance of the Baptism of Jesus; 3. list three importance of Baptism in the life of a Christian.

resources.title: The Temptation of Jesus.
resources.description: Theme: 1 THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. The temptation of Jesus Matt 4:1-11, Mk 1:12-13; Lk 4:1-13 2. The significance of the temptation of Jesus. 3. Temptations in the life of a Christian. 4. Ways of overcoming temptation: - Prayer - Be strong in your faith.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. narrate the story of the temptation of Jesus; 2. state the significance of the temptation of Jesus; 3. list some temptation in the life of a Christian; 4. mention ways of overcoming temptation
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on: - the temptation of Jesus; - the significance of the temptation of Jesus; - temptation in the life of a Christian; - ways of overcoming temptation.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion. 2. Ask and answer teacher’s questions. 3. Brainstorm on ways of overcoming temptations.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible pictures. 3. Charts. 4. Posters and films.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. narrate the three temptation of Jesus and His response to each; 2. give two significance of temptation of Jesus; 3. explain two ways a Christian can be tempted; 4. list four ways a Christian can overcome temptation.

resources.title: Call of the Disciples
resources.description: Theme: THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. Jesus calls His first four disciples. Matt.4:18-22; Mk.1:14-20; Lk.5:1-11. 2. Jesus calls the twelve Disciples/Apostles Mk.3:13-19 3. What it takes to be a disciple of Jesus Christ Matt.8:18-27; Lk.9:57-63; Lk.14:25-33. .
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. name the first four Disciples of Jesus; 2. give account of how they were called; 3. name the twelve Disciples; 4. state what it takes to be a disciple of Jesus.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussions on the call of the disciples and the gains of answering the call. 2. Leads class to dramatize the call of the four disciples. 3. Explains to students the different ways people are called to serve God today.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions. 2. Participate in dramatizing the call of the four disciples. 3. Mention people they know that answered the call of God.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible Pictures 3. Posters 4. Charts 5. Films showing how Jesus called the first four disciples and others.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give two reasons why Jesus called His disciples; 2. name the first four disciples of Jesus; 3. list the twelve disciples of Jesus; 4. List three demands of discipleship; 5. State what it takes to be a disciple of Jesus.

resources.title: Mission of the Disciples
resources.description: Theme: THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. Fishers of men. Matt.4:18-22, Lk.5:1-11 2. The preaching of Gospel and healing of the sick. Matt.10:1-15 3. The mission of the twelve apostle and the seventy disciples. Matt.10:1-15; Mk.6:7-13; Lk.9:1-16; Lk.10:1-24. 4. The outcome of the mission of the twelve and seventy disciples. Mk. 12; Lk.10:17-20.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state why Jesus called the disciples; 2. state the mission of the twelve disciples and the seventy disciples; 3. mention the outcome of the mission of the disciples; 4. describe the effect of the disciples’ activities on Nigerian Christians today.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussions on mission of Jesus’ disciples and the apostles. 2. Guides class to identify the effects of the mission of the disciples in Nigeria. 3. Leads class discussion on the problems to be faced when embarking on Christ’s mission. 4. Explain the difference between the apostle and disciples

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions. 2. Ask and answer teacher’s questions. 3. Students are to dramatize the duties of missionaries.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Posters 3. Bible pictures of the apostles 4. Charts
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give three reasons why Jesus called his disciples; 2. state three missions of the seventy disciples; 3. list five positive outcomes of the disciples work.

resources.title: Sermon on the Mount or the Beatitudes
resources.description: Theme: THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. The beatitudes. Matt.5:1-12 2. The Sermon on the Mount Matt. 5:13-16 - Forgiveness. Matt. 6:14-15. - Revenge. Matt. 5:38-42. - Fasting and Prayer. Matt. 6:5-13. - Love of money. Matt. 6:19-34 - Worrying Matt. 6:25-34.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. recite the beatitudes; 2. explain the Sermon on the Mount; 3. discuss Jesus teaching on forgiveness and revenge; 4. discuss Jesus’ teaching on: - prayer, - fasting, - anxiety - love of money.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on the teaching of Jesus on the Beatitudes. 2. Leads class discussion on Jesus teaching on Sermon on the Mount.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussions. 2. Study and memorize the beatitudes. 3. Read relevant Bible passages
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible Pictures 3. Posters, charts and films
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. recite meaningfully the beatitudes; 2. list two teachings of Jesus on Sermon on the Mount; 3. state why it is necessary to forgive your enemies; 4. explain the importance of prayer and fasting in a Christian’s life.

resources.title: Jesus’ Teaching in Parables
resources.description: Theme: THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. Meaning of parable. - Why Jesus taught in parables Matt. 13:34-35 2. Parables about the Kingdom: - The sower. Matt. 13:1-9, 18-23. - The wheat and Tares, Matt.13.24-30, 36-43, 3. Parable illustrating God’s love: - The prodigal son, Lk.15:11-32. - Lost sheep Lk. 15:3-7 - Lost coin. Lk. 15:8-10.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of Parables. 2. give reasons why Jesus taught in Parables; 3. narrate the categories of Jesus Parable with examples and its interpretations
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads discussion on: - meaning of parables, - reasons for use of parables by Jesus, - various parables of Jesus. 2. Discusses the use of proverbs among Nigerians.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Participate in class discussions. 3. Ask and answer teacher’s questions.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Posters 3. Bible pictures 4. Charts 5. Films
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give the meaning of parable; 2. list three reasons why Jesus taught in parables; 3. mention two parables each that teach: - God’s love for sinners, - about the Kingdom, - the right attitude to earthly possessions, maturity and responsibility. 4. Narrate one parable of Jesus.

resources.title: The Miracles of Jesus.
resources.description: Theme: THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. The meaning of miracle. 2. The Nature of the miracles of Jesus. - Turning water into wine. Jn. 2:1-11 - Calming the storm. Matt.8:23-27; Mk.4:35-41 - Feeding of the five thousand. Matt.14:13-21, Mk.6:30-44, Lk.9:10-17 - Feeding of the four thousand Mk.8:1-6.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of miracle; 2. give instances where Jesus demonstrated His power over nature; 3. explain the importance of faith in Jesus’ healing miracles; 4. narrate the story of Jesus feeding of the five thousand and four thousand people; 5. describe how Jesus demonstrated His power over death.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on the miracles performed by Jesus (Nature, healing and power over death) 2. Asks students to mention any miracle they have witnessed. 3. Leads class discussion on the miracles that borders on Christ having compassion on the needy.

Students: 1. Participate in discussions. 2. Actively discuss miracles they have witnessed in their lives and churches. 3. Read relevant Bible passages. 4. Describe people’s feelings on the loss of a loved one.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Posters 3. Bible pictures 4. Charts 5. Films 6. Slides. 7. Audio visual
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention three miracles in which faith in Jesus was demonstrated; 2. recount the feeding of the five thousand and four thousand; 3. give an instance where Jesus raised the dead.

resources.title: Jesus subjects Himself to Civil and Religious law.
resources.description: Theme: THE MINISTRY OF JESUS CHRIST | Content: 1. Jesus attitude to civil and religious law. Matt.5:17-20; Matt.22:15-22 - Jesus paid tax. Matt. 17:24-27. 2. Love as the supreme law. Jn.13:34-35; 1Cor.13:1 3. The qualities of love. Lk.2:51, 1Cor. 13:1-13.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state Jesus attitude towards civil and religious laws of His time; 2. recall when Jesus subjected Himself to civil and religious laws of His time; 3. identify love as the supreme law; 4. mention the advantages of showing love to their neighbours.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explain the importance of the law 2. Leads class discussion s. 3. Discusses the problem of a lawless society and benefits of laws in the society. 4. Discusses why Jesus made love the fulfillment of all the laws. 5. Discusses the consequence s of violating laws in Nigeria.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Debate on the importance of law in the society.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Posters 3. Bible pictures 4. Films
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain the meaning of civil and religious law; 2. list two civil and religious laws of Jesus’ time; 3. mention three laws of their society; 4. mention three occasions where Jesus had conflict with the leaders over the law; 5. list three advantages of loving ones neighbours.

resources.title: The passion of Christ
resources.description: Theme: THE PASSION, DEATH AND RESURRECTION OF JESUS | Content: 1. The Triumphant entry. Matt.21:1- 11, Mk.11:1-11, Lk.19:28-44. 2. The Last Supper. Matt.26:17-30 3. The Betrayal and Arrest. Mk.14:43-52, Matt.26:47-56 4. The Trial and Peter’s denial. Matt. 26:47-68, 69-75. 5. Instances which can lead a Christian to deny Christ and his/her neighbour.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. tell the story of the Triumphant entry of Jesus into Jerusalem and its significance; 2. recount the events that took place during the last supper; 3. give an account of the trial of Jesus and the denial by Peter; 4. state conditions that make a Christian deny Christ and one’s neighbour.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class to discuss the passion of Christ. 2. Guides students to discuss on what can make a Christian to deny Christ and his/her neighbour today.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Participate in class discussion.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Posters 3. Bible pictures 4. Films 5. charts
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state what happened during Jesus’ entry into the temple in Jerusalem; 2. recount two important events that took place during the last supper; 3. list two actions of a Christian that can constitute denial of Christ and neighbour; 4. tell the story of the trial of Jesus and denial by Peter.

resources.title: The Death and Burial of Christ
resources.description: Theme: THE PASSION, DEATH AND RESURRECTION OF JESUS | Content: 1. The Crucifixion. Matt.27:32-44 2. Jesus words on the cross. 3. The death. Matt. 27:45-56 4. The burial. Matt.27:57-61
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. tell the story of Jesus crucifixion; 2. recall the seven words of Jesus on the Cross; 3. state the events that heralded His death on the Cross; 4. give an account of His burial.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on Jesus crucifixion. 2. Guides students to dramatize Jesus’ crucifixion on the cross. 3. Guides students to memorize the seven words on the cross.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Dramatize the crucifixion of Jesus. 3. Memorize the seven words on the Cross.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Drama costumes 3. Posters 4. Bible pictures 5. Films 6. Charts 7. Audio- visual
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain why the day of Jesus, crucifixion is called Good Friday; 2. state the seven words of Jesus on the Cross; 3. state three notable events that happened at the death of Jesus; 4. state where Jesus was buried and by who.

resources.title: The Resurrec- tion and Appearance
resources.description: Theme: THE PASSION, DEATH AND RESURRECTION OF JESUS | Content: 1. The Resurrection. Matt.28:1-10; Mk.16:1-8; Lk.24:1-12 2. Appearances Matt.28:16- 20; Mk.16:9- 18; Jn.21:1- 14 and Lk. 24:13-49. 3. Significance of Jesus resurrection to the Christians.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. tell the story of resurrection of Jesus; 2. state various appearances of Jesus after His resurrection; 3. state the significance of Jesus resurrection to Christians.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussions on the resurrection and the appearances of Jesus. 2. Guides students to dramatize the resurrection story.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Dramatize the resurrection story. 3. Participate in class discussion on resurrection. 4. Ask and answer teacher’s questions.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Drama costume. 3. Posters 4. Charts 5. Film 6. Video and Bible pictures.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state two significance of Jesus appearance when Thomas was present; 2. state two significance of Jesus’ resurrection for the Christians; 3. mention the first person to see the resurrected Jesus.

resources.title: The Ascension of Christ.
resources.description: Theme: THE PASSION, DEATH AND RESURRECTION OF JESUS | Content: 1. The Great Commission. Matt.28:16- 20, Mk.16:15- 18 2. Jesus ascends into heaven. Matt.16:19- 20, Lk.24:50- 53. 3. Signs that will accompany those who will spread the gospel.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the great commission; 2. describe how Jesus was taken into heaven. 3. list the signs that will accompany those who will obey the great commission.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on the Ascension of Christ. 2. Discuses on the great commission. 3. Guides them to list the signs that will follow them that spread the gospel.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Bring Costumes from their homes. 4. Dramatize Jesus’ ascension.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Drama costumes. 3. Films. 4. Charts 5. Posters. 6. Bible pictures.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state the Great Commission; 2. list four signs that will follow those who carry out the Great Commission; 3. state what the Angel said concerning the ascending Jesus; 4. state where the ascension of Jesus took place; 5. explain two roles Christians of today play in the great commission.

resources.title: The promise of the Holy Spirit
resources.description: Theme: THE BEGINNING OF THE CHURCH | Content: 1. The promise of the Holy Spirit. Jn.14: 26 Jn.15:26 Acts.1:3-5 2. The coming of the Holy Spirit. Acts 2:1-13. 3. Peter’s first speech and its effect. Acts 2:14-41.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. discuss the importance of Jesus’ promise of the Holy Spirit to the disciples; 2. narrate the story of the fulfillment of the promise; 3. give account of Peter’s speech on the Pentecost day and its effects.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read appropriate Bible passages. 2. Leads in the discussion and summarizes Peter’s speech.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Copy summary into their notes.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Charts showing tongues of fire on the heads of the disciples.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain why Jesus promised the Holy Spirit to the disciples; 2. mention the visible and audible signs of the coming of the Holy Spirit; 3. state the reactions of the on lookers; 4. mention how many persons were converted as a result of Peter’s speech on the Pentecost day.

resources.title: Fellowship in the Early Church.
resources.description: Theme: THE BEGINNING OF THE CHURCH | Content: 1. Social and religious life of the early church. - Togethernes s in the early church. Acts 2:41- 47; 5:1-11 - Murmuring in the early church. Acts 6:1-2 2. Selection of Deacons. Acts 6:1-7, (equitable distribution). 3. Comparison of the early church to present church.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. describe the social and religious life of the early church; 2. mention the qualities of a deacon; 3. compare the life of the early Christians and the Christians today.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read relevant Bible passages. 2. Leads discussion on the social and religious life of the early church. 3. Guides students to identify the name and function of the Deacons. 4. Teacher guides students on group discussion on the life of the early church and the Christians today.

Students: 1. Listen and participate in reading the relevant Bible passages. 2. Write names of the Deacons in their notes. 3. Copy from chalkboard summary on the functions of the Deacons. 4. Brainstorm on the differences between the early church and the church today.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Word cards containing the names of the Deacons.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state three activities which the early church did together; 2. state two reasons why the widows of Hellenist murmured; 3. name the seven Deacons; 4. list three functions of Deacon; 5. state three differences between the early church and the Christians today.

resources.title: Opposition to the Gospel Message.
resources.description: Theme: THE BEGINNING OF THE CHURCH | Content: 1. Arrest of Peter and John. Acts 3:11-44, 4:5- 31. 2. Arrest and Martyrdom of Stephen. Acts 6:8-17, 1-60 3. Persecution of the church by Saul. Acts 8:1-3, 9:1-43 4. Martyrdom of James. Acts 12:1-3.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. give reasons for the arrest of the apostles; 2. summarize Stephen’s defense; 3. give examples of opposition to the Christian faith in their churches and communities.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read the relevant Bible passages. 2. Guides students in identifying reasons for the arrest of Stephen, Peter and John. 3. Writes out key issues in Stephen’s defense.

Students: 1. Listen and participate in class discussion. 2. Read the Bible passages. 3. Role-play.
resources.resources: 1. The Bible 2. Pictures/ Almanac showing martyrdom of saints. 3. Students as learning resources.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. give three reasons for the arrest of Peter and John; 2. mention what Stephen said in his defense about the following: - The temple - The law; 3. give two examples of acts of opposition in their different churches;

resources.title: The Ministry of Peter.
resources.description: Theme: THE BEGINNING OF THE CHURCH | Content: 1. Peter and Simon the Magician. Acts 8:14-25. 2. Healing miracles of Peter: - Raising of Dorcas. Acts 9:32-42 3. The conversion of Cornelius. Acts 10:1-48 - Peter defends his action in Cornelius’ house. Acts 11:1-18 4. Peter’s divine release from prison and death of Herod. Acts 12:1-24
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. relate the story of Peter’s encounter with Simon the magician; 2. narrate the story of the raising of Dorcas (Tabitha); 3. state the significance of the conversion of Cornelius 4. give an account of the release of Peter from Prison.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Describes vividly Peter’s encounter with Simon the magician. 2. Guides students to role-play the raising of Dorcas. 3. Guides students to role-play the conversion of Cornelius. 4. Narrates the story of the divine release of Peter from prison.

Students: 1. Listen attentively and participate in class discussion. 2. Participate in the role-playing. 3. Read the Bible passage. 4. Copy note from the chalkboard.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible 2. Students as learning resources. 3. Audio- visual
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. narrate the story of Peter’s encounter with Simon the magician, 2. tell the story of the raising of Dorcas (Tabitha); 3. state the significance of the conversion of Cornelius; 4. tell the story of the release of Peter from prison.

resources.title: Some Teachings of St. Paul
resources.description: Theme: THE LIFE AND TEACHINGS OF PAUL | Content: 1. Paul’s teachings on: - Dignity of Labour. 2Thess. 3:6- 15,Col.3:23 - Obedience to constituted authority. Rom. 13:1-7, Eph. 6:5-8 - Love. 1Cor.13, Rom.13:18-10 2. Types of work people do. 3. Why people should do their work with honour. 4. Need to obey constituted authority.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. mention some of the teachings of St. Paul; 2. state the meaning of dignity of labour; 3. identify various types of work people do; 4. state why they should do their work with honour; 5. state why it is necessary to obey constituted authority; 6. state why they should show love to one another.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class debate on “No Job is more important than the other”. 2. Encourages students to demonstrate how to show love to their neighbours. 3. Shows picture of people of different professions. 4. Leads class discussions on student’s ambition in life.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Listen and participate in the discussion. 3. Class debates on importance of one job to the other. 4. Bring gifts to share with their class mate as evidence of practical love.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Pictures of people of different profession.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. mention two different types of work; 2. enumerate three ways of showing respect to constituted authority; 3. give four reasons why we must love our neighbours; 4. list six characteristic of dignity of labour: - punctuality - honesty - commitment - hard work - cooperation.

resources.title: Paul’s Trials
resources.description: Theme: THE LIFE AND TEACHINGS OF PAUL | Content: 1. Paul’s arrival at Jerusalem and arrest. Acts 21:17-40 2. Paul before the Jewish Council (Sanhedrin) and the plot to kill him. Acts 22:30-33; 35 3. Paul before Roman Governors (Felix, Festus and Agrippa) and his appeal to Rome. Acts 25:1-21; Felix; Acts 24:1- 27; Felix Acts 25:22; Agrippa Festus; Acts:25:13-14.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. state the accusations that led to Paul’s arrest; 2. state the cause of the division among the members of the Council; 3. give the reason for Paul’s appeal to Caesar; 4. state how Paul’s case revealed the weaknesses of those in authority.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on the passage read. 2. Leads students to discuss the accusation leveled against Paul, 3. Discuss Paul’s defence before Roman Governors.

Students: 1. Read relevant Bible passages. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Ask and answer teacher’s questions. 4. Copy the chalkboard summary.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible. 2. Bible pictures 3. Posters 4. Charts
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list the accusation leveled against Paul; 2. list the two major parties of the Sanhedrin; 3. state why there was division among the members of the Sanhedrin; 4. State why Paul appealed to Caesar in Rome.

resources.title: The Growth of the Church
resources.description: Theme: THE CHRISTIAN CHURCH TODAY | Content: 1. The Great Commission. Matt.28:19-20, Mk.16:15-16. 2. Marks of growth in the church e.g. organizing crusades, revivals, vigils, prayer meetings, miracles, etc. Acts 2:1-47
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. relate the evangelisation efforts of the church.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads students to discuss the evangelisation efforts of the church. 2. Guides students to list evidence of church growth.

Students: 1. List some of the religious activities they had attended. 2. Memorize the Great Commission in Mathew 28:18-20.
resources.resources: 1. Films on revivals, crusades, prayer meetings and worship. 2. The Holy Bible 3. Recorded audio tapes on sermons. 4. Paper cutting on religious gatherings. 5. Pictures of people, cathedrals, big churches and small churches. 6. Drama Costumes.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. state three activities carried out during evangelism; 2. list three factors responsible for the growth of churches respectively; 3. list three prominent church leaders in Nigeria today.

resources.title: Unity Among Christians
resources.description: Theme: THE CHRISTIAN CHURCH TODAY | Content: 1. Christian organizations in Nigeria e.g. Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN), etc. 2. Definition of inter- denomination and their activities. 3. Christian giving. Phil.4:14-20; 2Cor.8:3-5; 2Cor.9:6-15; 4. Teachings that will foster unity. Jn. 17:15, 21. - Faith/Works. Jam. 2:14-18. - Humility. Phil. 2:3- 11, 1Pet.5:5-11; - Impartiality. Jam. 2:1-13; - Forgiveness Gal.6:1-2, etc.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. list some Christian organizations in Nigeria. 2. discuss inter- denomination al activities in our churches today. 3. identify Biblical teachings towards unity of purpose. 4. practice Christian assistance to one another in times of need.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides class to read relevant passages. 2. Leads class to demonstrate how to love one another. 3. Asks and answers questions on Christian giving.

Students: 1. Read relevant passages. 2. Give gifts to their friends. 3. Bring Costumes from their houses.
resources.resources: 1. Drama costumes. 2. Pictures of people working and worshiping together. 3. Pictures of Christians holding meeting. 4. Films of joint programmes. 5. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. list any two Christian Organizations in Nigeria. 2. mention two inter- denomination al activities in our churches today. 3. state three attitude among Christians that will foster unity. 4. state why a Christian should render assistance to another Christian in need.

resources.title: Christians Living among Non- Christians
resources.description: Theme: THE CHRISTIAN CHURCH TODAY | Content: 1. Christian living in the community. 1Pet.1:3-17, 2, Matt.5:13-16. 2. Christian attitude to persecution. 1Pet.3:13-17, James 1:12-15, 1Pet. 1:6-9; 9 and 10. 3. Discussion on Christian’s attitude to non-believing authorities.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the expected attitudes of Christians to non- Christians in society; 2. Christian attitude to constituted non-Christian authorities; 3. describe Christian attitudes to persecution.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides students to read the passages. 2. Directs a play on Christian living among non- Christians. 3. Asks questions on persecution of Christians. 4. Leads discussion on Christian’s attitude to unbelieving leaders.

Students: 1. Read Bible passages. 2. Dramatize a play on Christian living among non- Christians. 3. Assess the negative effect of persecution on believers. 4. Write a letter to a Christian friend in Nigeria where Christians are constantly persecuted.
resources.resources: 1. The Holy Bible 2. Pictures of churches burnt or vandalized during religious crises. 3. Christian magazines showing the persecution of Christians in some parts of the world. 4. Drama materials.
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain how to encourage Christians to remain faithful when tribulations come their way; 2. list two nature of persecution meted out to Christians in your area; 3. mention five points of advice from the passages on how Christians should live in the community; 4. list Christian attitudes to unbelieving leaders.

resources.title: Peaceful co- existence
resources.description: Theme: THE CHRISTIAN CHURCH TODAY | Content: 1. Explanation of peaceful coexistence i.e. living in peace with others. Matt.5:21-25. - Instances in the Bible of people desiring peaceful coexistence e.g. Esau and Jacob. Gen. 31:1-11; Gen. 13:1-8, 26:26-29; - Philemon and Onesimus, Phil. 1:1- 30 - Isaac and Abimelech. (Gen.26:2-29) 2. Demonstration of how people can show desire for peaceful co- existence, e.g. call for dialogue, tolerance, forgiveness, call for reconciliation or settlement of disputes. 3. Origin of Christianity and Islam from Abraham as one father. Gen.16:15-16; Gen.21:1-3.
resources.objectives: Students should be able to: 1. explain the term peaceful co-existence; 2. list/enumera te instance of people desiring peaceful co- existence in the Bible; 3. identify reasons for wanting peaceful coexistence; 4. explain the origin of Christianity and Islam as being of one father (Abraham).
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of peaceful coexistence. 2. Explains the reasons for peaceful coexistence. 3. Enumerates the ways of creating peaceful coexistence 4. Explains the problems arising from lack of peaceful coexistence (violence, war).

Students: 1. Ask question. 2. Demonstration of peaceful coexistence by sharing and working together in the classroom.
resources.resources: 1. Picture showing people settling land, religious and community disputes. 2. The Holy Bible
resources.assessment: Students to: 1. explain peaceful coexistence; 2. give two examples of those who quarreled but later lived peacefully; 3. list two reasons why people should have desire for peaceful coexistence; 4. mention two ways to create peaceful coexistence.
